rows.explanation: The note gives inputs, a Medium confidence and a reason, and most inputs (SMP-001/002/005-008, 033) do support 'every wafer' coverage that offsets sparse sampling. But Micron (SMP-025) speaks only of 'improve sampling efficiency' (which could mean fewer physical measurements) and never of every-wafer coverage. 'Memory front end' also mislabels Intel's SMP-033, which is logic or unspecified front end.
rows.suggested_fix: Change the label to 'Front end (memory and logic)'. Reword to 'SK hynix and Intel present VM/AI as extending coverage to every wafer and offsetting sparse physical sampling; Micron cites improved sampling efficiency without a number; none discloses a % cut in physical measurements in period'.

rows.found_wording: These techniques utilize reduced sampling plans ... The implementation of 100% overlay measurement is needed ... This paper will highlight the development of C2W overlay metrology at Intel, with an emphasis on its roadmap
rows.explanation: The Intel + EV Group abstract (Intel affiliation shown in the Crossref record) blames reduced sampling on current C2W systems inherited from litho/W2W in general, not on an Intel practice, and presents 100% measurement as a development concept on a roadmap, so 'Intel's move' overstates it. 'The only in-period chipmaker statement' also ignores TALK-022, an Intel-organised VLSI 2025 hybrid-bonding workshop that calls for 'ultra-dense sampling'. The note does give inputs, Low confidence and a reason.
rows.suggested_fix: Reword: 'Hybrid-bonded logic: the main in-period chipmaker statement on sampling intensity is the Intel + EV Group ECTC 2026 abstract, which argues that 100% chiplet bond-overlay measurement is needed instead of the reduced-sampling plans of inherited C2W tools and presents a development concept (roadmap, not HVM). An Intel-organised VLSI 2025 workshop also lists ultra-dense sampling as a need (TALK-022). No TSMC SoIC or Foveros Direct production sampling statement was found or retrievable.' Add TALK-022 and MAIN-006 to the inputs.

rows.found_wording: Intel describes ... their use of Streaming Scan Network (SSN), High-bandwidth IJTAG (HB-IJTAG), and generic data streaming (GDS) technology ... significantly reduced their overall test application time
rows.explanation: Samsung's 'up to 75% (3.9 times faster)' (SEM image throughput) and ASE's 'decreases significantly SAM scanning time' (AI image enhancement in FA) are supported. Intel's test-time cut in SMP-032, however, comes from DFT streaming technologies (SSN, HB-IJTAG, GDS), and the abstract does not mention AI, so listing it as an AI time saving is wrong. The wording 'Quantified AI time savings' also clashes with two of the three items being unquantified. Other in-period AI time-saving rows are left out: SMP-004 (SK hynix, defect-analysis time, unquantified) and SMP-024 ([C] Micron, 1 million work hours a year).
rows.suggested_fix: Reword: 'In-period AI time savings stated by the chipmakers apply to image acquisition or FA (Samsung SEM, up to 75% / 3.9x, SMP-017; ASE SAM scan time, unquantified, SMP-037; SK hynix defect-analysis time, unquantified, SMP-004) or to enterprise manufacturing ([C] Micron, SMP-024), not to the number of HBM production inspections. They do not reverse the abstract's description of the models being applied during in-line monitoring. So the abstract contains no words showing that the row overstates it. The note already says "abstract only; full text NOT RETRIEVED", which marks the limit. The [F] tag fits: this is a fact read in an official abstract record dated 2025-05-05, which is inside the period. Whether another row should use this as evidence of production status (for example SYN-028's "production" class) is a separate question for that row.
